meta.name: First coming
meta.blurb: Old Testament passages the New Testament says were fulfilled in Jesus’ birth, ministry, death and resurrection.

meta.name: Who he is
meta.blurb: Passages where the New Testament applies the LORD’s own words and titles, including “the first and the last” and “Alpha and Omega”, to Jesus.

meta.name: Second coming
meta.blurb: Old Testament pictures of the Lord’s coming, judgment and new creation, and how the New Testament, especially Revelation, takes them up.

items.title: A prophet like Moses
items.text: Peter (Acts 3:22–23) and Stephen (Acts 7:37) quote Moses’ promise of a prophet “like unto me” and apply it to Jesus.
items.christian: Christians read this promise as pointing to Jesus as the prophet greater than Moses.

items.title: A son of David on an everlasting throne
items.text: Luke 1:32–33 says God will give him “the throne of his father David”. Hebrews 1:5 quotes 2 Samuel 7:14: “I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son.”
items.christian: Christians read the promised son of David as the Messiah, fulfilled in Jesus.

items.title: “Thou art my Son”
items.text: Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5; 5:5 quote Psalm 2:7: “Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.”
items.christian: Christians read the royal Son of Psalm 2 as the Messiah, Jesus.

items.title: The sign called Immanuel
items.text: Matthew 1:22–23 says this happened “that it might be fulfilled” and quotes Isaiah 7:14, adding that Emmanuel means “God with us”.
items.christian: Christians read the birth of Jesus as the fulfilment of this sign.

items.title: Light in Galilee
items.text: Matthew 4:14–16 says Jesus’ move to Capernaum happened “that it might be fulfilled” and quotes Isaiah 9:1–2 about Zabulon, Nephthalim and “a great light”.
items.christian: Christians read the light in Galilee as Jesus’ ministry.

items.title: A voice in the wilderness
items.text: All four Gospels apply Isaiah 40:3, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness”, to John the Baptist, who prepares the way for Jesus.
items.christian: Christians read John the Baptist as the forerunner of the Messiah.

items.title: A ruler from Bethlehem
items.text: Matthew 2:5–6 quotes Micah 5:2 when Herod asks where the Christ was to be born: “In Bethlehem of Judaea”.
items.christian: Christians read the ruler from Bethlehem as Jesus.

items.title: A king on a donkey
items.text: Matthew 21:4–5 says the colt ride happened “that it might be fulfilled” and quotes Zechariah 9:9.
items.christian: Christians read the entry into Jerusalem as the coming of the promised king.

items.title: Forsaken, and the garments divided
items.text: Matthew 27:46 records Jesus crying the words of Psalm 22:1 on the cross. John 19:24 says the soldiers casting lots for his coat happened “that the scripture might be fulfilled” (Psalm 22:18).
items.christian: Christians read Psalm 22 as describing the suffering of the Messiah.

items.title: The suffering servant
items.text: Matthew 8:17, John 12:38, Acts 8:32–33 and Luke 22:37 each quote Isaiah 53.
items.christian: Christians read the servant as Jesus, suffering for others.

items.title: “They shall look upon him whom they pierced”
items.text: John 19:37 says “another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced”, quoting Zechariah 12:10.
items.christian: Christians read the piercing as the crucifixion.

items.title: Not left to see corruption
items.text: Peter (Acts 2:27, 31) and Paul (Acts 13:35) quote Psalm 16:10, “neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption”, as speaking of the resurrection.
items.christian: Christians read the verse as foretelling Jesus’ resurrection.

items.title: “Sit at my right hand”
items.text: Jesus quotes Psalm 110:1 in Matthew 22:44; Peter (Acts 2:34–35) and Hebrews 1:13 quote it too.
items.christian: Christians read the verse as the Messiah’s exaltation.

items.title: The rejected stone
items.text: Jesus (Matthew 21:42), Peter (Acts 4:11) and 1 Peter 2:7 quote the stone that the builders rejected becoming the head of the corner. (The KJV of Psalm 118:22 says “refused”.)
items.christian: Christians read Jesus as the rejected stone made cornerstone.

items.title: The messenger who prepares the way
items.text: Jesus says John the Baptist is the one of whom Malachi 3:1 speaks: “Behold, I send my messenger before thy face” (Matthew 11:10).
items.christian: Christians read the messenger as John the Baptist.

items.title: A new covenant
items.text: Hebrews 8:8–12 quotes Jeremiah 31:31–34 at length. At the Last Supper Jesus calls the cup “the new testament in my blood” (Luke 22:20).
items.christian: Christians read the new covenant as established through Jesus and the church.

items.title: Out of Egypt
items.text: Matthew 2:15 quotes Hosea 11:1, “Out of Egypt have I called my son”. In Hosea the verse begins “When Israel was a child, then I loved him”.
items.christian: Christians read Matthew as applying Israel’s story to Jesus (a typological reading).

items.title: The Spirit poured out
items.text: On the day of Pentecost Peter says “this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel” (Acts 2:16) and quotes Joel 2:28–32.
items.christian: Christians read Pentecost as the beginning of the church and the fulfilment of Joel.

items.title: “I am the first and the last”
items.text: In Isaiah 44:6 the LORD says “I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.” In Revelation 1:17–18 and 2:8 the risen Christ says he is “the first and the last”. Revelation 22:13 reads “I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last”; Revelation 1:8 and 21:6 also use “Alpha and Omega”.
items.christian: Christians read Jesus as taking a title the LORD claims in Isaiah, which they take as a claim to deity (source 7).

items.title: Every knee shall bow
items.text: Isaiah 45:23 has the LORD say “unto me every knee shall bow”. Philippians 2:10–11 says every knee should bow “at the name of Jesus” and confess “that Jesus Christ is Lord”. Romans 14:11 quotes the Isaiah verse about standing before God’s judgment seat.
items.christian: Christians read Paul as applying the LORD’s own words to Jesus.

items.title: Calling on the name of the LORD
items.text: Joel 2:32 says “whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered”. Romans 10:13 quotes it (“shall be saved”) right after 10:9, “confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus”.
items.christian: Christians read Paul as applying a text about the LORD to Jesus.

items.title: Words addressed to the Son
items.text: Hebrews 1:8 addresses the Son with Psalm 45:6, “Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever”, and 1:10–12 applies Psalm 102:25–27, “Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth”, to him.
items.christian: Christians read these as statements of the Son’s deity and his role in creation.

items.title: Isaiah saw his glory
items.text: John 12:41 says “These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him”, after quoting Isaiah 6:10. In Isaiah 6:1 the prophet sees “the Lord sitting upon a throne”.
items.christian: Christians read John as saying Isaiah saw Jesus’ glory.

items.title: “Art thou the Christ?”
items.text: Asked if he is “the Christ, the Son of the Blessed”, Jesus answers “I am” and speaks of the Son of man “coming in the clouds of heaven” (Mark 14:61–62, echoing Daniel 7:13). The high priest calls it blasphemy (14:63–64).
items.christian: Christians read Jesus’ answer as a claim to share God’s authority and glory.

items.title: “Before Abraham was, I am”
items.text: In Exodus 3:14 God says “I AM THAT I AM” and “I AM hath sent me unto you”. In John 8:58 Jesus says “Before Abraham was, I am”, and verse 59 says “then took they up stones to cast at him”.
items.christian: Christians read this as Jesus claiming the divine name.

items.title: “Mighty God” and “God with us”
items.text: Isaiah 9:6 gives the child the names “The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace”. Matthew 1:23 says Emmanuel means “God with us”. Luke 1:32–33 speaks of “the throne of his father David” and a kingdom with no end.
items.christian: Christians read Isaiah 9:6 as naming the Messiah as divine (source 6).

items.title: In the beginning
items.text: Genesis 1:1 and John 1:1 both begin “In the beginning”. John 1:1 says “the Word was God”, 1:3 says “All things were made by him”, and 1:14 says “the Word was made flesh”.
items.christian: Christians read John as presenting Jesus as the Word through whom creation came.

items.title: “Me whom they have pierced”
items.text: In the KJV the LORD says “they shall look upon me whom they have pierced” (Zechariah 12:10). John 19:37 quotes it as “him whom they pierced”, and Revelation 1:7 as “they also which pierced him”.
items.christian: Christians read the LORD who speaks in Zechariah as the one who is pierced, and John applies it to Jesus.

items.title: Coming with the clouds
items.text: Daniel 7:13 sees “one like the Son of man” come “with the clouds of heaven”. Matthew 24:30 says “the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven”, and Revelation 1:7 says “Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him”.
items.christian: Christians read these as pointing to Jesus’ return in glory (sources 10, 11).

items.title: Every eye shall see him
items.text: Revelation 1:7 joins Daniel 7:13 with Zechariah 12:10: “every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him”, and “all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him”.
items.christian: Christians read the mourning as the response of the nations to Jesus’ return (source 11).

items.title: Feet on the Mount of Olives
items.text: Zechariah 14:3–4 says the LORD “go forth” and “his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives”. In Acts 1:11–12 the angels say Jesus “shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven”, and the disciples return from “the mount called Olivet”.
items.christian: Many Christians read Zechariah 14:4 as the place of Jesus’ return (source 12).

items.title: “My reward is with me”
items.text: Isaiah 40:10 says “his reward is with him”. Revelation 22:12 says “Behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me”. The wording is closely parallel.
items.christian: Reading the echo as one coming, the LORD’s in Isaiah and Jesus’ in Revelation, is a Christian interpretation.

items.title: The rod of iron
items.text: Psalm 2:9 says “Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron”. Revelation 2:27, 12:5 and 19:15 use “rod of iron”.
items.christian: Christians read these passages as the Messiah’s rule at his return.

items.title: Death swallowed up
items.text: 1 Corinthians 15:54 quotes “Death is swallowed up in victory” (Isaiah 25:8). Isaiah 25:8 also says the Lord GOD “will wipe away tears from off all faces”; Revelation 21:4 says “God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”.
items.christian: Christians read the end of death as the result of Jesus’ resurrection and return.

items.title: A new heaven and a new earth
items.text: Isaiah 65:17 says “I create new heavens and a new earth”. 2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1 speak of “a new heaven and a new earth”.
items.christian: Christians read this as the renewal of creation after Jesus’ return.

items.title: River and tree of life
items.text: Revelation 22:1–2 describes “a pure river of water of life” and “the tree of life” whose leaves are “for the healing of the nations”. Ezekiel 47:12 speaks of trees with “the leaf thereof for medicine”, and Genesis 2:9 names “the tree of life”.
items.christian: Christians read Revelation as restoring the garden and the river of Ezekiel’s vision.

items.title: The dead raised
items.text: Daniel 12:2 says “many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. John 5:28–29 says “all that are in the graves shall hear his voice” and come forth to “the resurrection of life” or “the resurrection of damnation”.
items.christian: Christians read Jesus as the one who raises the dead at the end.

items.title: The sun darkened
items.text: Matthew 24:29 says “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light” before the Son of man comes. Isaiah 13:10 says “the sun shall be darkened in his going forth” and Joel 2:31 “The sun shall be turned into darkness”.
items.christian: Christians read these as signs connected with Jesus’ return.

items.title: The first promise
items.text: In Genesis 3:15 God tells the serpent: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Paul writes that God sent his Son “made of a woman” (Galatians 4:4) and that “the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly” (Romans 16:20).
items.christian: Since Irenaeus (about 180), Christians have read this verse as the first promise of the Messiah, the “protoevangelium” or first gospel: the woman’s seed is Christ, the bruised heel is the cross, and the crushed head is his victory over Satan (source 13).
items.views: In rabbinic Judaism the “seed of the woman” is usually read as all of humankind, not one person, and no clear messianic reading of the verse is known from before Christianity. The New Testament does not quote Genesis 3:15 directly; the passages above echo it (source 13).

items.title: God will provide a lamb
items.text: Abraham tells Isaac, “God will provide himself a lamb” (Genesis 22:8), and a ram caught in a thicket is offered in Isaac’s place (22:13). John the Baptist says of Jesus, “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world” (John 1:29), and Peter speaks of “the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish” (1 Peter 1:19).
items.christian: Christians read the ram given in Isaac’s place as a picture of substitution, and Abraham’s words as pointing to Jesus, the Lamb God himself provides (source 14). Mount Moriah is traditionally linked with the later Temple Mount in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 3:1), a tradition rather than a settled fact (source 14).
items.views: The New Testament never quotes Genesis 22:8 when it calls Jesus the Lamb, so this is a pattern Christians see (a “type”), not a prophecy the New Testament quotes.

items.title: The Passover lamb
items.text: The Passover lamb had to be “without blemish”, its blood was put on the doorposts, and “neither shall ye break a bone thereof” (Exodus 12:5–7, 46). John says the soldiers did not break Jesus’ legs, “that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken” (John 19:36). Paul writes, “Christ our passover is sacrificed for us” (1 Corinthians 5:7).
items.christian: Christians read the spotless, unbroken Passover lamb as foreshadowing Jesus, who died at Passover time and whose blood saves, as the lamb’s blood saved Israel in Egypt (source 15).
items.views: The rule about bones appears in Exodus 12:46 and Numbers 9:12, and something similar in Psalm 34:20, so readers link John 19:36 to more than one passage.

jv.31054: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.
jv.31055: And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
jv.31056: And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.
jv.31057: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
jv.31059: And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.
jv.31081: And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.
jv.31082: In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
jv.31083: And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him:
jv.31084: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads.
jv.31085: And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.
jv.31092: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.
jv.31093: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.
